newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine starts assembling GAZ cars.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine starts assembling GAZ cars.

text.p: Russia's second largest carmaker GAZ has started producing cars and vans in Ukraine's Crimean peninsula, a company official said on Thursday.

Anatoly Lazarev, chief executive of KrymavtoGAZservis, a joint venture between GAZ and a local company, told Reuters that 1,200 GAZ-3110 Volga cars and more than 2,000 GAZEL vans will be assembled by the end of the year at the Simferopol plant.
The new assembly line with 5,000-car annual capacity was launched on Wednesday, he added. Lazarev also said that the plant aimed to produce 1,500 GAZ-3110s next year.

"It's enough so far to meet the demand in Ukraine," Lazarev said, adding that production will be aimed largely at the Ukrainian market. The Volga saloons will have a price tag of 27,000 hryvnia ($14,500) in Ukraine.
Both cars and vans have engines from Britain's Rover Group, a subsidiary of Germany's BMW AG and Japan's Toyota Corp, Lazarev said.
Two months ago Crimean officials said they had reached agreement with South Korean carmaker KIA Motors to assemble three KIA models at a plant in the eastern Crimean town of Feodosiya.
It is still not clear when the project with 10,000- 20,000-car annual capacity will start.

South Korea's unlisted Daewoo Group won a tender to produce cars at Ukraine's AvtoZAZ car manufacter in the eastern city of Zaporizhya. Daewoo has formed a joint venture with U.S. carmaker General Motors for the AvtoZAZ project with annual capacity of 250,000-300,000 cars.
